scenarios.scenario_title: Wedding photo with cousin vs virtual ceremony screenshot (Search Abandonment)
scenarios.raw_text:
User wanted to see pictures of a wedding in which she was with her cousin physically however she got the photo where user was not physically there it was her sister’s wedding ceremony in which she was in virtual call and there was one screenshot of her being in the call.
User searched - wedding
Workaround - user scrolled first but she was not able to get that photo. Then she wrote HALDI and scrolled but was unable to retrieve. Then user wrote YELLOW SUIT then also the same result eventually user wrote CEREMONY and still was unable to find that picture.
Result being user abandoned the search
And complaints she know she has that photo and will eventually find it if scrolls manually but it will take much time so lets skip
[ user skipped the thought that if the photo has her cousin inside it why not directly search with cousin’s name or by simply writing my photo with my cousin]
After being told she tried but still was unable to find that picture. Result - complete abandonment
scenarios.debrief_note: User failed to find the photo in second scenario after being asked what do you think is preventing you from finding it? User replied: tried many key words to find the picture but was unable to get that, maybe the problem is to find the right keyword to actually get the right picture. And one more thing after trying so many times and still not getting the asked photo, user got pissed off and exited google photos.
scenarios.target_photo: Wedding photo where user was physically present with her cousin.
scenarios.initial_memory_clue: Physical wedding presence with cousin; Haldi ceremony; yellow suit worn.
navigation_steps: Searched 'wedding' -> received screenshot of virtual video call instead of physical attendance.
Scrolled manually without success.
Searched cultural sub-event 'HALDI' and scrolled -> not found.
Searched visual clothing clue 'YELLOW SUIT' -> not found.
Searched broader event synonym 'CEREMONY' -> not found.
Prompted by interviewer to try cousin's name and 'my photo with my cousin' -> still failed.
User rage-quit and exited the app.
scenarios.result_position: Not found in top results; irrelevant screenshot surfaced first.
scenarios.grid_or_scroll_depth: Multiple grids scrolled across 6 query iterations.
scenarios.job_to_be_done: Differentiate and retrieve photos from an in-person wedding event with a cousin versus virtual call screenshots
scenarios.research_interpretation: Severe retrieval failure: user knows photo exists, attempts 6 query reformulations (event, ceremony stage, clothing color, person name, relational prompt), faces irrelevant video-call screenshots, experiences extreme frustration and exits app.
scenarios.situation_description: Attempting to retrieve physical wedding ceremony pictures with a cousin, differentiating from virtual attendance screenshots.
scenarios.what_user_remembers: Being physically at her sister's wedding with her cousin, Haldi ritual, wearing a yellow suit.
scenarios.retrieval_clue_used: Event 'wedding', ritual 'HALDI', attire 'YELLOW SUIT', ceremony 'CEREMONY', person 'cousin's name', relationship 'my photo with my cousin'.
scenarios.what_they_tried: Attempted 6 successive keyword and natural language searches, scrolling deeply after each attempt.
scenarios.what_happened: Google Photos returned irrelevant virtual call screenshots; target photo never surfaced.
scenarios.workaround_or_outcome: Complete abandonment: user stated manual scrolling would take too long, became frustrated ('pissed off'), and exited the app.

scenarios.scenario_title: Building watchman lighting diya at gate (Face clustering threshold failure & multi-object anchor)
scenarios.raw_text:
Wanted photos of her building's watchman, who she'd photographed once during Diwali when he lit a diya at the gate.
Went directly to People & Pets tab first — his face wasn't indexed as a separate person (grouped under "unnamed faces" cluster, buried).
Gave up on the tab, searched — diya gate
Got the photo, 2nd grid, Best Match.
She noted: "If I hadn't remembered Diwali, I don't think I'd have found this. The People tab was useless here because he's not someone I photograph often enough for it to learn his face properly."
scenarios.debrief_note: She noted: 'If I hadn't remembered Diwali, I don't think I'd have found this. The People tab was useless here because he's not someone I photograph often enough for it to learn his face properly.'
scenarios.target_photo: Single photo of building watchman lighting a festival oil lamp (diya) at the building gate during Diwali.
scenarios.initial_memory_clue: Building security guard / watchman, photographed only once during Diwali, lighting a diya at the gate.
navigation_steps: Went directly to 'People & Pets' tab to search by face.
Face was missing from indexed people groups; buried inside unorganized 'unnamed faces' cluster.
Abandoned tab navigation.
Typed contextual multi-object query: 'diya gate'.
Found photo in 2nd grid under Best Match.
scenarios.job_to_be_done: Find a one-off photograph of an acquaintance / service worker not frequently photographed
scenarios.research_interpretation: Critical systemic limitation: Facial recognition models require frequency thresholds to promote faces into searchable person entities. Infrequent contacts (watchmen, delivery workers, one-off interactions) are permanently lost to facial search. Retrieval was rescued solely by multi-object spatial co-occurrence ('diya gate').
scenarios.situation_description: Locating a one-off photo of a building watchman taken during Diwali.
scenarios.what_user_remembers: Building watchman lighting a diya at the main gate during Diwali.
scenarios.retrieval_clue_used: Facial lookup -> spatial multi-object query 'diya gate'.
scenarios.what_they_tried: Navigated People & Pets tab, abandoned upon discovering unindexed face, searched 'diya gate'.
scenarios.what_happened: Face tab failed completely; multi-object search surfaced photo in 2nd grid.
scenarios.workaround_or_outcome: Rescued via spatial-object context when face identification failed.
